page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.8-128 is a flexible compute instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The instance is configured with 8 dedicated physical CPU cores supporting simultaneous multithreading, providing 16 virtual CPUs (vCPUs). Backed by 128.0 GB of system memory, the instance delivers a memory-to-vCPU allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU, placing it in a memory-dense operational profile.

The instance configuration includes no bundled local storage, requiring persistent workloads to rely on external network-attached block volumes. It also contains no discrete GPU hardware accelerators. For networking and external access, the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Resource sizing reflects a flexible configuration where dedicated core capacity is paired with substantial memory density without the overhead of unused accelerator hardware.

Given the ratio of 8.0 GB of memory per vCPU and dedicated AMD EPYC compute cores, this shape is suited for memory-intensive applications that do not depend on high-speed ephemeral local NVMe scratch space. Typical target workloads include in-memory caching layers, medium-scale relational databases, ETL batch pipelines, and backend application servers requiring expansive memory working sets.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.8-128 is a memory-dense compute instance based on the x86_64 architecture. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor running at 2.7 GHz, it provides 8 physical cores and 16 dedicated vCPUs alongside 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or GPU accelerators, relying on remote block storage for persistence. It comes equipped with one complimentary public IPv4 address. The dedicated core distribution and elevated memory density offer cost-effective scaling for memory-bound tasks without provisioning unneeded physical accelerators. VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.8-128 is well suited for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, such as in-memory caches, distributed processing engines, relational database instances, and data transformation pipelines.
